audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.28%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.43%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Passiamo ai mercati occidentali. L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dell'1.08%, il VIX è in aumento del 2.93%. Il Dollar Index è in calo dello 0.08%, l'euro/dollaro è a 1.14, in calo dello 0.37%. L'oro è a 4183 dollari l'oncia, in calo dello 0.97%. Il petrolio Brent è a 79.12 dollari, in calo dello 0.91%. Il rendimento del decennale americano è in aumento, mentre il BTP 10Y è stabile al 3.82%.

Sul fronte geopolitico, la Banca d'Inghilterra ha mantenuto i tassi di interesse a 3.75%. La situazione in Ucraina continua a rappresentare una sfida fiscale e finanziaria. Inoltre, l'apertura del canale di Hormuz non risolverà le vulnerabilità energetiche chiave dell'Europa.

Infine, sul fronte macro, nessun dato rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin scende del 2,60% a sessantadue mila trecentosessanta dollari. I flussi degli ETF mostrano un deflusso netto di ottantadue milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dinamiche del mercato.

Le altcoin mostrano perdite più significative. Ethereum scende del 3,12% a mille seicento ottantotto dollari, Solana perde il 4,93% a sessantotto virgola ventisei dollari e BNB scende del 3,00% a cinquecentosettantuno virgola cinquantotto dollari.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a quattordici, in zona di Extreme Fear. Questo livello suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 0.28%, while Shanghai fell 0.43%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets. Let's pivot to the Western markets. The S&P 500 closed up 1.08%, and the VIX is up 2.93%. The Dollar Index is down 0.08%, and the euro/dollar is at 1.14, down 0.37%. Gold is at $4,183 per ounce, down 0.97%. The Brent oil price is $79.12, down 0.91%. The 10-year US yield is rising, while the 10-year BTP is stable at 3.82%. On the geopolitical front, the Bank of England kept interest rates at 3.75%. The situation in Ukraine continues to pose a fiscal and financial challenge. Furthermore, the reopening of the Hormuz channel will not solve Europe's key energy vulnerabilities. Finally, on the macro front, there are no significant data releases today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin falls 2.6% to $62,360 The ETF flows show a net outflow of $82 million. This movement could be influenced by recent market dynamics. Altcoins show more significant losses. Ethereum falls 3.12% to $1,688, Solana loses 4.93% to $68.26, and BNB falls 3% to $571.58 The Fear & Greed Index is at 14, in the Extreme Fear zone. This level suggests caution among investors. No macro data is scheduled for today. To delve deeper into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Even Hormuz reopening will not resolve Europe’s key energy vulnerability
articles.snippet: Even Hormuz reopening will not resolve Europe’s key energy vulnerability Expert comment thilton.drupal 18 June 2026 Europe remains over reliant on insecure and persistently expensive natural gas. It should focus efforts on reducing demand. European governments, most of which rely on oil and gas imports to fuel their economies, have been nervously watching prices climb and storage levels fall in the weeks since the US-Israeli attack on Iran triggered the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. They could be forgiven for being relieved by this week’s news of a US-Iran framework agreement that promises to enable ships to transit the Strait, through which approximately one-fifth of oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) flowed before the war. articles.title: Stablecoin remuneration on centralised exchanges
articles.snippet: by Wenqian Huang, Nikola Tarashev, Xinyi Wang Centralised exchanges remunerate stablecoin holders, using the return on the issuer's reserve assets or income from market activity. Under the reserve-based model, yields track policy rates – akin to yields on cash-management instruments – whereas under the activity-based model, yields are much more volatile. By turning stablecoins into substitutes for bank deposits or money market funds or into funding instruments for exchanges' risky activities, remuneration models may shape the macro financial implications of wide stablecoin adoption in the future.

articles.title: Good Medicine Is Combat Power: Clinical Innovation and the Lessons of the Russo-Ukrainian War
articles.snippet: War is a brutal driver of medical innovation. Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has forced clinicians and commanders alike to confront a hard truth: Survival depends not only on tactics and technology, but on the ability to deliver advanced care under fire, evacuate and resuscitate the wounded, and preserve fighting strength despite repeated attacks on healthcare systems.Ukraine’s experience has reshaped combat medicine through necessity, resilience, and improvisation. articles.snippet: Analysts are back to expecting a huge oil glut next year as they see the U.S.-Iran deal as the end of the worst of the Middle East crisis. The deal is actually just the beginning of long processes of negotiations, a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, recovery of the more than 13 million barrels per day (bpd) of shut-in oil production in the Middle East, and a world so low on inventories – except in China – that refilling these will support oil prices for months to come.
